sections.heading: Problem
paragraphs: Per the file, solana's initial RPC implementation (per the file) was created for the purpose (per the file) of allowing users to confirm txs that had just recently been (per the file) sent to the cluster. Per the file, it was designed with (per the file) memory usage in mind such that any node ought to be able to support (per the file) the API without concern of DoS attacks. Per the file, later down the line, (per the file) it became desirable to (per the file) use that same API (per the file) to support the Solana explorer.

Per the file, the original design only (per the file) supported minutes of history, (per the file) so we changed it to instead store tx statuses in a local (per the file) RocksDB instance and offer days of history. Per the file, we then extended that (per the file) to 6 months via BigTable. Per the file, with each modification, the (per the file) API became more suitable (per the file) for applications serving static (per the file) content and less appealing for tx processing.

Per the file, the clients poll for tx status instead of being (per the file) notified, giving the false (per the file) impression of higher confirmation times. Per the file, furthermore, what clients can (per the file) poll for is limited, (per the file) preventing them from making (per the file) reasonable real-time decisions, including recognizing a tx is confirmed as soon as particular, known nodes vote on it. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Proposed Solution
paragraphs: Per the file, a web-friendly, tx-oriented, streaming API built around the node's ReplayStage. Per the file, improved client experience: Support (per the file) connections directly from WebAssembly apps. Per the file, clients may be notified of confirmation (per the file) progress in real-time, including (per the file) votes and voter stake weight. Per the file, clients may be notified when the (per the file) heaviest fork changes, if it affects the txs confirmation count. Per the file, easier for nodes to support: Each node supports some number of (per the file) concurrent connections and otherwise (per the file) has no significant resource constraints.

Per the file, transaction status is never (per the file) stored in memory and (per the file) cannot be polled for. Per the file, signatures are only stored (per the file) in memory until the (per the file) desired commitment level or (per the file) until the blockhash expires, whichever is later. Per the file, how it works: The client connects to a node using a reliable communication channel, including a web socket. Per the file, the node registers the signature with ReplayStage. Per the file, the node sends the tx into the Gulf Stream (per the file) and retries all known (per the file) forks until the blockhash (per the file) expires (not until the tx is accepted on only the heaviest fork).

Per the file, if the blockhash expires, (per the file) the signature is unregistered, (per the file) the client is notified, (per the file) and connection is closed. Per the file, as ReplayStage detects events affecting the tx's status, it notifies the (per the file) client in real-time. Per the file, after confirmation that the tx is rooted (CommitmentLevel::Max), the (per the file) signature is unregistered and the (per the file) server closes the upstream channel. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.
